scenes.title: One drop. An endless journey.
scenes.narration: The water in your glass has been on an extraordinary journey. It moves between oceans, the air, and land in a repeating water cycle.

scenes.title: It starts with the sun.
scenes.narration: The sun supplies energy that warms water in rivers, lakes, and oceans. Some liquid water becomes invisible water vapour and enters the air.

scenes.title: Liquid becomes vapour.
scenes.narration: This change is called evaporation. It happens at the surface, even without boiling. Plants also release water vapour through tiny openings in their leaves.

scenes.title: Cooling creates clouds.
scenes.narration: When moist air cools enough, water vapour condenses onto tiny particles. Countless little water droplets or ice crystals gather together to form clouds.

scenes.title: Water returns to Earth.
scenes.narration: Inside clouds, droplets and ice particles can grow. When conditions allow them to fall, water returns as precipitation, including rain, snow, or hail.

scenes.title: Many paths. One cycle.
scenes.narration: Some water flows over land into rivers and oceans. Some soaks into the ground. Water can remain stored for a while before moving again.

scenes.title: The journey keeps going.
scenes.narration: The sun powers evaporation, cooling helps clouds form, and gravity brings water back down. The water cycle connects the sky, the land, and us.
